- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward bias.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or increase slope sensitivity.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply lagged correction or dampen momentum in forecast.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., rapid drop from high to low), model often fails to recognize it; add decay factor or use moving average smoothing.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of downside risk; consider adding volatility buffer or downward shift for negative sentiment periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread trend direction; use sentiment-weighted moving average to anchor forecast.
